subject: Recap: Nexalus discovery — portability, success criteria, and next steps
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: John Dawson <john.dawson@nexalus.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: Nexalus discovery — portability, success criteria, and next steps

John / Maya — thanks again for taking time today. Short recap below so we’re aligned and have a clear path forward. If anything is off, call it out and I’ll update the MPA (mutual plan of action).

Key pain points you called out
- Cost volatility from 3rd-party LLM provider spikes (OpenAI overage months).
- Latency and tail spikes when traffic peaks (customer-facing chat).
- Blackbox safety checks: current Anthropic step adds latency and complicates chaining.
- Data residency and encryption controls for PHI workflows.

Current stack you described
- Production: OpenAI chat completions (gpt-4.1) for conversational UI; Anthropic for post-filtering/safety checks.
- Hosting: mix of cloud-hosted microservices in GCP (us-west1) with a thin proxy to the external APIs.
- Volume: ~120M tokens/month average, spiking to ~300M in peak months.

Success criteria you want to measure (we captured these)
- Latency: p50 < 250ms, p95 < 800ms for end-to-end generation (including safety filter).
- Cost: target blended per-1k-token cost <= $0.75 at projected scale.
- Quality: top-3 intent classification parity within ±2% vs current baseline.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 evidence, KMS/HSM integration, and ability to keep inference within customer VPC in a private deployment.
- Rollout safety: canary and automatic fallback to Anthropic/OpenAI if quality or latency regress.

Initial shortlist and compatibility notes (what we suggested on the call)
- Llama-2 70B quantized (on-host) — good latency when properly compiled; concerns about quantization on long-context tokens.
- Mistral-Instruct class — promising cost/quality for instruction tasks; need tokenizer parity checks.
- Redwood-curated open variants (we will provide perf profiles) for parity testing.

Immediate next steps (owners and ETA)
1) Compatibility checklist (we attach the checklist): IR (Irene) — deliver today.
2) Technical deep-dive (network, tokenization, KV cache) — propose 60–90 min session with your infra and security teams next week. ACTION: please confirm availability 11/17–11/19.
3) SOC2 / security package & custom cost model — Ben will prepare SOC2 artifacts and a 12-month cost projection by 11/12.
4) POC scope: lightweight on-prem-compatible POC using a 10M token monthly baseline for 4 weeks — we’ll propose a POC plan after deep-dive.

Attachments: call recording (20261110-call_recording-nexalus.mp3), compatibility checklist (nexalus-compatibility-checklist-20261110.xlsx), and a short POC outline (redwood-poc-outline.pdf).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the deep-dive once you confirm the preferred window.

— Irene Choi
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

On Tue, Nov 10, 2026 at 09:05 AM John Dawson <john.dawson@nexalus.com> wrote:
> Great conversation this morning, Irene. Appreciated the clarity on the fallback patterns.
> — John
From: John Dawson <john.dawson@nexalus.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@nexalus.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: Nexalus discovery — portability, success criteria, and next steps

Irene — thanks for the crisp summary. A few clarifications from our side:
- Priority ranking: 1) Security/compliance (SOC2 + KMS), 2) Cost predictability, 3) Latency consistency.
- Timeline: procurement window opens mid-December; ideal POC start by 01/15/2027.
- Consumption estimate to share: we expect steadier growth — current run-rate 120M tokens/mo, planning for 250M tokens/mo by Q3.

Ask: can you send an SOC2 evidence packet (even a stubbed scope and auditor name) and a short example of a fall back configuration that still preserves safety checks? Also please include a rough POC acceptance criteria list so procurement has something to review.

If those items are available by 11/12 it would be very helpful for our procurement sync next week.

— John
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: John Dawson <john.dawson@nexalus.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: Nexalus discovery — portability, success criteria, and next steps

John — thanks, noted and appreciate the timeline. Quick responses inline and next-actions: 

- SOC2 packet: Ben will attach a SOC2 evidence summary and our auditor contact. Ben (cc) — can you target EOD 11/12 for the packet?
- Fallback config: we’ll document a fallback topology that routes to Anthropic/OpenAI with circuit-breakers and per-route sampling for quality checks. I’ll include a one-page diagram in the Drive folder.
- POC acceptance criteria: draft in the attached POC outline; we’ll make it procurement-friendly (clear pass/fail thresholds).

Proposed deep-dive: Tue 11/17 11:00–12:30 PST (60–90 min). If that doesn’t work, please propose two windows. I’ve added a provisional calendar link: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=tech-deep-dive-nexalus

Drive: shared folder with checklist + POC outline: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cNexalusSharedFolder

Thanks — Irene

To: John Dawson <john.dawson@nexalus.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: Nexalus discovery — portability, success criteria, and next steps

John / Team — Ben here (security & pricing). I’ll assemble: 
- a condensed SOC2 evidence packet with scope + auditor contact (pdf stub attached soon),
- a 12-month cost projection for the 120M -> 250M token profile, and
- a short note on KMS/HSM integrations and VPC private deployment steps.

Expecting to drop those artifacts into the Drive and the HubSpot deal record (https://hubspot.com/contacts/DEAL-2026-0921-NEXA) by EOD 11/12. If procurement needs a signed letter of intent or an NDA before the POC, flag it and we’ll move legal.

— Ben
